title: The American lawn has a gen z problem: ScottsMiracle-Gro CEO
summary: Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi sits down with ScottsMiracle-Gro CEO Nate Baxter to discuss why the 160-year-old brand is radically reinventing itself as a "lifestyle" company.

title: The Cash Machine The Market Put On Sale: LOW
summary: The home improvement giant is generating far more cash than the median S&P 500 company, yet the market keeps walking away. Here’s the offer, the catch, and the one number that will settle the debate.

title: Home Depot (HD) Brings Magic Apron AI Assistant To All U.S. Stores
summary: Home Depot (NYSE:HD) has rolled out its Magic Apron AI shopping assistant across all U.S. stores. The Magic Apron tool offers real-time project guidance, product location, and expert advice through the Home Depot app and in store QR codes. Customers and associates can access multi language support and image recognition to help match projects with the right materials and tools. The nationwide deployment marks a wider use of artificial intelligence inside physical home improvement retail...

title: What Could Lift Walmart Stock Is Not On Its Shelves
summary: The retailer keeps cutting shelf prices, and profit is growing far faster than the U.S. comp, with almost half of that growth coming from areas like advertising, marketplace, and membership.

title: Prediction: Home Depot’s Turnaround Could Be Bigger Than Investors Expect
summary: Home Depot just flashed its clearest turnaround signal in two years, yet the stock sits 20% below its 52-week high while analysts pile on buy ratings. Here is why the market may still be sleeping on what comes next.

title: Home Depot vs. Lowe’s: One Housing Recovery Play Stands Out
summary: Both Home Depot and Lowe's are fighting the same frozen housing market, but their Q2 earnings reveal a widening gap between two very different strategies. One company is gaining ground while the other is quietly retreating.

title: Tariffs Hurt Williams-Sonoma More Than the Housing Market
summary: Williams-Sonoma  stock dropped on Wednesday even though the home specialty retailer delivered a beat-and-raise quarter in tough times for housing.  The stock is up 25% this year, but down 11% from its all-time closing high of $251.78 on Aug. 7, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  While other retailers are logging tariff refunds, Williams-Sonoma is feeling a sting.

title: Home Depot Stock's Upside Case Now Runs Through A Business It Bought
summary: The distribution arm inside Home Depot has gone from dragging comparable sales down to comping above the company average, and that shift is the clearest upside lever left while housing stays frozen.

title: Williams-Sonoma Stock Dips Despite Q2 Earnings and Revenue Beat
summary: WSM beats fiscal Q2 earnings and revenue estimates and raises its 2026 outlook, but shares dip as tariffs pressure adjusted margins.

title: How big box retailers are using tariff refunds
summary: Walmart is investing its $2.9 billion return into price cuts, while Target plans for additional reimbursements and Home Depot and Lowe’s offset higher costs.
